name: Marchigiano

ancestors.notes: Central Italian parent, with Southern influences in the south of the region.

notes: Marchigiano. Central Italian of the Marche region. Transitional zone: northern Marche is closer to Romagnol (Gallo-Italic), central Marche is Central Italian, southern Marche is closer to the Neapolitan continuum. Reference: central Marche (Macerata). Key features: (1) 7-vowel system. (2) Metaphony in southern varieties. (3) Assimilatory processes (Loporcaro 2009, Avolio 1995). GRAPHEMES: the grapheme table and its positional readings come from it-IT through graphemes_base, because the variety writes standard Italian spelling. ⟨c g⟩ read [tʃ dʒ] before ⟨e i⟩ and [k ɡ] elsewhere: cielo [ˈtʃɛːlo], gelo [ˈdʒɛːlo] (Bertinetto & Loporcaro 2005, JIPA 35(2), p. 133). ⟨i u⟩ before a vowel are the glides [j w]: pieno [ˈpjɛːno], chiave [ˈkjaːve], guida [ˈɡwiːda] (p. 139, Table 2 on p. 138). The spec keeps its own ⟨s⟩ and ⟨z⟩ readings and does not take the it-IT positional ones: the it-IT intervocalic [z] and word-initial [dz] are the Standard Northern values, and no source for this variety was opened.

sources.author: Bertinetto, P.M. & Loporcaro, M.
sources.title: The sound pattern of Standard Italian, as compared with the varieties spoken in Florence, Milan and Rome
sources.publisher: Journal of the International Phonetic Association
sources.notes: JIPA 35(2). Illustration of Standard Italian; states the preconsonantal /s/ voicing agreement and documents the Tuscan/Northern split in intervocalic ⟨s⟩. Table 2 (p. 138) and p. 139 give the opening and closing diphthongs and the hiatus that the stress diphthongs list follows; p. 137 gives the two equal vowels in hiatus.
